# Frontend API

Routes are relative to `/api/care_ccn_be/` and follow CARE EMR conventions: snake_case JSON, EMR error bodies and
paginated lists. Every FE route needs an authenticated user. Permissions are not implemented yet: any authenticated
user can read and act on every transaction.

## Routes

Each action is its own API, contributed by a mixin on the flow's viewset. `referral` has discover, select, init,
confirm and status; `appointment` has all seven actions.

| Method | Path | Body / query | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `bap/<flow>/` | `?transaction_id=&status=&contract_id=&coordination_id=&limit=&offset=` | paginated `BecknTransactionListSpec` |
| `GET` | `bap/<flow>/{transaction_id}/` | | `<Flow>TransactionRetrieveSpec` |
| `POST` | `bap/<flow>/discover/` | `BapDiscoverSpec` | `202 BapActionResponseSpec` |
| `GET` | `bap/<flow>/{transaction_id}/catalogs/` | | `BapCatalogsSpec`, the catalogs of every `on_discover` |
| `POST` | `bap/<flow>/{transaction_id}/<action>/` | `bap_<action>_spec` of the flow | `202 BapActionResponseSpec` |
| `GET` | `bap/message/` | `?transaction_id=` (required) `&action=on_select&direction=in` | paginated `BecknMessageReadSpec` |
| `GET` | `bpp/<flow>/`, `bpp/<flow>/{transaction_id}/` | as for `bap/<flow>/` | Care-as-BPP transactions |
| `GET` | `bpp/message/` | as for `bap/message/` | |

The ONIX routes are unchanged: `POST bap/receiver[/on_<action>][/]` and `POST bpp/receiver[/<action>][/]`.

## Request bodies

Every action body:

- may include `context` overrides, remembered for later actions: `network_id`, `version`, `bpp_id`, `bpp_uri`,
  `ttl`, `schema_context`. Other keys are ignored. Send `bpp_id` / `bpp_uri` once, at `select`, from the chosen
  catalog. They are dropped on discover, which always goes to the discovery service;
- may include a raw Beckn `message` (passthrough), validated against the flow's schema. The builder is skipped and
  the flow's `perform_<action>` side effects still run. Required fields only apply without a passthrough `message`;
- is rejected with `400` if it contains unknown fields or is not a JSON object.

| Spec | Fields (`*` required without a passthrough `message`) |
|---|---|
| `BapDiscoverSpec` | `health_service_type`, `acceptance_mode`, `text_search`, `filters` |
| `ReferralSelectSpec` | `offer_id*` |
| `ReferralInitSpec`, `ReferralConfirmSpec` | `facility*` (uuid), `patient` (uuid) or `patient_name`, `encounter` (uuid), `title`, `reason`, `category`, `offer_id`, `assigned_facility_id`, `emergency`, `priority`, `questionnaire` (uuid), `questionnaire_response` |
| `AppointmentSelectSpec` | `resource_id*`, `offer_id`, `date`, `health_service_type` |
| `AppointmentInitSpec` | `slot_id*`, `patient*` (uuid) |
| `AppointmentConfirmSpec` | `slot_id*`, `patient*` (uuid), `coordination_ref` |
| `AppointmentRescheduleSpec` (`update`) | `slot_id*` |
| `AppointmentCancelSpec` | `reason` |
| `BapActionSpec` (`status`) | only `context` / `message` |

### Automatic referral file synchronization

Completed Care uploads with `file_type="referral"` and `associating_id` set to a network-linked referral's UUID
are automatically attached as `source` resources and synchronized after commit. Existing attachments keep their
category. No separate Beckn update call is required: the origin sends `update`, and the assigned instance sends
`on_update`. Files explicitly shared as referral resources also synchronize when their upload completes.

The other instance downloads the signed file URL into its own storage and attaches a local copy to the matching
referral. Imported files are marked to prevent echoing them back; incomplete, deleted and archived files are not sent.
Origin updates wait for confirmation. Both instances must run Celery workers, and each must configure
`BECKN_ARTIFACT_ALLOWED_HOSTS` to allow the other instance's storage host. Signed URL lifetime and download size
are controlled by `BECKN_ARTIFACT_URL_TTL` and `BECKN_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES`.
This synchronization covers file uploads and completed referral questionnaire responses. Other shared clinical
records, such as diagnostic reports, are not currently synchronized.

```json

```

Retrieve the transaction to follow it:

```json

  "id": "…", "transaction_id": "a9046a23-…", "adapter": "bap", "flow": "appointment",
  "status": "ON_CONFIRM", "network_id": "…", "counterparty_id": "…", "counterparty_uri": "…",
  "contract_id": "…", "coordination_id": "", "last_error": null,
  "routing": {"bap_id": "…", "bap_uri": "…", "bpp_id": "…", "bpp_uri": "…"},
  "context": {"bpp_id": "…", "bpp_uri": "…"},
  "actions": ["DISCOVER", "ON_DISCOVER", "SELECT", "ON_SELECT", "CONFIRM", "ON_CONFIRM"],
  "patient": null, "facility": null, "created_by": {…},
  "confirm": {"slot_id": "…", "patient": "…"},
  "created_date": "…", "modified_date": "…"
}
```

- `status` starts at `QUEUED`, becomes `<ACTION>` once ONIX ACKs the request and `ON_<ACTION>` when the callback
  arrives. `NACK` and `ERROR` carry `last_error`; a missing caller URL is `ERROR` with `last_error.code =
  "NOT_CONFIGURED"`.
- Referral transactions also carry `referral_id`, the origin Care `Referral`.
- For BAP referral detail and action routes, the origin referral UUID can also be used in place of
  `{transaction_id}`. Responses and network messages still contain the original transaction ID. This allows the
  referral's network status panel to find transactions created through discovery as well as Care-created referrals.
- On a successful `on_confirm`, `contract.contractAttributes.referral.id` is saved on the referral link as the
  remote referral ID, separately from `contract.id`. Subsequent automatic `update` messages include that remote

  If the callback does not include a remote referral ID, updates omit it for compatibility.

| Case | Response |
|---|---|
| Invalid body (spec) | `400 {"errors": [<pydantic errors>]}` |

## Issue: Re-picking a network provider skips `select` on the new discover transaction

**File:** `/Users/nandkishorr/work/care/care_fe/src/components/Referral/CreateReferralDialog.tsx:716-731`. The same problem affects `networkAvailability` and `networkSelected` at lines 367-381, and the form key at line 868.

**Severity:** High

**Problem:** The dialog uses `NetworkOffer.key` to tell offers apart, but the key isn't unique across searches. `extractNetworkOffers` builds it from array positions (`${messageIndex}-${catalogIndex}-${offerIndex}`, `src/types/ccn/ccn.ts:282`). When the user clicks **Change destination**, `NetworkDestinationSearch` mounts again. Its `lastDiscovered` ref starts empty, so it runs a new `discover` and gets a new transaction ID, and the keys start over at `"0-0-0"`.

Here is a common way to hit it:
1. The user picks provider X. Its key is `0-0-0` on transaction T1, and `select` on T1 succeeds or is still pending.
2. The user clicks **Change destination**. A new discover returns transaction T2.
3. The user picks the first result again: the same provider, or any provider listed first. Its key is also `0-0-0`.

What happens next:
- `sameOffer` is true, so `selectOffer(offer)` is skipped and `select` is never sent on T2.
- `networkSelected` and `networkAvailability` still match on `variables.key`. The UI shows the form and availability from T1 as if this offer were selected.
- On send, `submitNetworkReferral` calls `init` and `confirm` on `offer.transactionId`, which is T2. T2 never had a `select`, so it has no selected availability. The backend will reject it with 70006/70007 or a flow error.
- If the new first offer is a different facility, the body also carries the wrong `questionnaire` and `assigned_facility_id` from T1.
- The `ReferralQuestionnaireForm` key doesn't change, so answers from the old form are kept.

If the first `select` is still pending when this happens, it later resolves for T1 and marks the T2 offer as selected.

**Evidence:**
- Keys are built from indices in `extractNetworkOffers`.
- `ReferralDestinationPicker` (with its `network` search) only renders while `choosingDestination` is true, so it mounts fresh each time the user opens it.
- The `lastDiscovered` ref resets on that remount, so a new discover runs every time.
- Inside `NetworkDestinationSearch`, the selected-state check (`isSelected`) compares `offerId` and `bpp_id`. That confirms `key` is only a React list key, not an identity.
- The current Playwright spec has a single offer at `0-0-0`, so this path would collide every time if the spec re-picked a destination.

**Suggested fix:** Compare offers by identity that includes the transaction, such as `transactionId + offerId + context.bpp_id`, or by object reference (`selectMutation.variables === networkOffer`). Use it for `sameOffer`, `networkAvailability`, and `networkSelected`, and in the `ReferralQuestionnaireForm` key. You could also make the key itself include `transactionId`.

I've updated the CCN referral flow in care_fe to match the new section of `care_ccn_be/docs/fe_api.md` (availabilities and their forms). Type-check (`npx tsc --noEmit`) and the CCN unit tests (7/7) pass. I updated the Playwright network-referral spec but didn't run it: its setup resets the local backend database from a snapshot, which would wipe your local data. Nothing has been tested against a live CCN backend yet.

**How sending a network referral works now**
- **Picking a provider** now sends `select` straight away and waits for `on_select`. The transaction then includes the receiving facility's `availability` and its forms.
- **The receiving facility's request form** appears in the dialog using the same form component as local referrals. If there are several request forms you can choose one; if there are none, the dialog says so. The answers also appear on the review screen.
- **Sending** now calls `init` first, which only checks the request, then `confirm`, which creates the referrals. Both carry the same body, including `questionnaire` and `questionnaire_response`. The facility (`assigned_facility_id`) and referral category now come from the selected availability when it has them.
- **Errors 70005, 70006 and 70007** now show specific messages, whether they come back as a `400` from the action or as the transaction's `last_error`. If a 70007 doesn't name specific questions, the form has changed on the other side, so a "Reload the form" button runs `select` again.

**Files changed**
- [ccn.ts](/Users/nandkishorr/work/care/care_fe/src/types/ccn/ccn.ts): new types for the availability, its forms, the form fields on `init`/`confirm` and `last_error.paths`, plus the error codes and two small helpers.
- [networkReferral.ts](/Users/nandkishorr/work/care/care_fe/src/components/Referral/network/networkReferral.ts): the new `select` step, the `init` → `confirm` send, and reading the error codes.
- [CreateReferralDialog.tsx](/Users/nandkishorr/work/care/care_fe/src/components/Referral/CreateReferralDialog.tsx): loading the form after picking a provider, form rendering, review, error messages and the reload button.
- [en.json](/Users/nandkishorr/work/care/care_fe/public/locale/en.json): new strings added. I removed `ccn_sending_select`, which nothing uses any more.
- **Tests:** [ccn.test.ts](/Users/nandkishorr/work/care/care_fe/src/types/ccn/ccn.test.ts) has two new unit tests. [referral-network.spec.ts](/Users/nandkishorr/work/care/care_fe/tests/facility/referrals/referral-network.spec.ts) now mocks `init` and the `on_select` availability with a real form, fills the form, and checks the `init` and `confirm` bodies.

A code review caught one bug, now fixed: picking a provider again after a new network search could skip `select` on the new search. Offers are now matched by search, offer and provider rather than by list position.

**Known limitations**
- If a remote form uses a dropdown list that doesn't exist on this Care instance, the form shows "choices unavailable".
- When the receiving facility rejects specific answers, the message names them, but those questions aren't highlighted in the form.
